# Grove Directory

Grove Directory is a curated, health-aware developer directory powered by
the Grove framework. The directory is a structured, blueprint-aware
mirror of every record in the showcase — every entry carries the
metadata a developer needs to decide whether to open the source.

## Important pages

- Home: https://example.com/
- Browse: https://example.com/projects
- About: https://example.com/about
- Contributors: https://example.com/contributors
- Submit a record: https://example.com/submit
- Trending: https://example.com/projects?label=hot
- Recently added: https://example.com/projects?label=new
- Established: https://example.com/projects?label=mature
- Browse by stack: https://example.com/projects
- Browse by category: https://example.com/projects

## What the directory contains

- Real, runnable open-source records (projects, resources, entities)
- Stack, language, and architecture at a glance
- Activity, health signals, and maturity tiers
- License, stars, and contribution readiness
- Curated notes: best for, why listed, caveats
- Filters by stack, platform, license, and status

## Data layout

- `data/records/*.yml` — human-edited source of truth
- `data/taxonomy/*.yml` — categories, stacks, platforms, channels
- `data/generated/records.*.json` — build-time projection
- `data/generated/site-config.json` — blueprint + site metadata

## How it's built

The static site is rendered by Astro, fed by JSON projections
produced by `@grove-dev/cli generate` from the YAML records. The
build chains:

1. `pnpm run build:data` — yml → JSON
2. `pnpm run build:sitemap` — emit public/sitemap.xml
3. `pnpm run build:llms` — emit public/llms.txt + llms-full.txt
4. `astro build` — render the static site
